verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe Mem0 Open Source as the same memory engine as the Platform, running on your own infrastructure. They also document a self-hosted Docker stack that bundles the REST API, a dashboard, per-user API keys and an audit log. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted Docker deployment, and evidence of the source repository, license and detailed deployment steps.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Mem0 Open Source is the same memory engine as the Platform, running on your own infrastructure. You own the stack, the data, and every component
As a self-hosted server. A Docker stack with a dashboard, per-user API keys, and a request audit log.
Self-host Mem0 with full control over your infrastructure and data
Stand up the Mem0 REST server and dashboard in a few minutes, with an admin account, API keys, and a live audit log included.
